failure_reason: Tier-1 HTTP (curl_cffi, rotating chrome profiles) reached https://www.shopterrain.com/sale-home and https://www.shopterrain.com/sale-garden successfully, but the very next request (https://www.shopterrain.com/sale-outdoor-living) returned 403 on every one of 6 curl_cffi browser profiles (chrome116/119/123/124/131/133a) simultaneously - a hard DataDome block on the host, not a single bad profile. Per the access-tier rule ('the first block stops that host'), no further requests were made to shopterrain.com after that, including no escalation to Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome for this same host in this same session, since the block hit mid-pagination and further probing would only burn more attempts against an active block. As a result, 3 confirmed sibling child slugs of the Sale nav node (sale-outdoor-living, sale-gifts, sale-furniture) plus 2 more listed child slugs of uncertain nature (limited-time-sale, free-home-shipping-event) could not be opened or verified, even though their existence is confirmed from the site's own nav data (see notes).
notes: Navigation discovery: top-level shop-by-category nav (superNav.navItems['shopping-root'] in the homepage Pinia state) includes a 'Sale' item (slug 'shop-sale', displayName 'Sale'), whose primary rendered URL is /sale-home (categoryId SHOP-SALE, displayName '**All Sale', SEO title 'New Markdowns | Home + Garden Sale'). No separate /clearance, /outlet, /last-chance, or /final-sale URL exists - all 404'd (confirmed before the block, these are clean 404s, not blocks). SALE VS CLEARANCE JUDGMENT: the page is customer-facing-labelled 'Sale' (H1 'Sale'), not 'Clearance', which per the brief would normally argue against inclusion. However the site's OWN backend category config for this exact node explicitly sets allowPermanentMarkdownTiles=true AND allowTemporaryMarkdownTiles=false - i.e. the site's own taxonomy classifies this as a permanent-markdown category, the opposite of a temporary promotional campaign (compare: the New-Arrivals category has the reverse flags, allowTemporaryMarkdownTiles=true/allowPermanentMarkdownTiles=false, confirming this field pair is how the platform itself distinguishes temporary vs permanent markdown merchandising). The on-page SEO copy also frames it as 'New Markdowns' and ongoing stock-clearing ('After the holidays have ended, stock up on celebratory decor for next year's celebrations... new markdowns'), consistent with permanent clearance-style merchandising rather than a dated campaign (no Black-Friday/seasonal-campaign framing seen). On balance this is recorded as genuine Clearance-type merchandising, flagged MANUAL REVIEW given the customer-facing 'Sale' label, per the brief's explicit guidance to record-but-flag rather than guess. GENUINE SUB-STRUCTURE CONFIRMED (not a duplicate/facet re-cut): the /sale-home node's own navItem.childSlugs = ['limited-time-sale','free-home-shipping-event','sale-home','sale-garden','sale-outdoor-living','sale-gifts','sale-furniture']. Opened /sale-garden before the block hit: it has its own breadcrumb chain (shop-sale > sale-garden), its own categoryId, and totalRecordCount=24 with 24 distinct productIds on a single page - genuinely different product set from sale-home's 23 (sale-garden is a superset-in-size but not a literal subset judging by spot-checked SKUs, e.g. TR-107671158-000 'Floral Arch Handle Basket Planter' appears in BOTH sale-home and sale-garden, confirming real overlap/co-listing rather than either being a total aggregate of the other - both kept per the 'overlap is expected, not an error' rule). sale-outdoor-living, sale-gifts, and sale-furniture are near-certainly parallel department-specific Sale listings (same naming/structural pattern as sale-garden, same parent, same categoryId family) but were NOT opened, so no qty row is emitted for them per the brief's 'only valid once you open it and confirm' rule - inventing rows for unopened candidates would risk a fabricated-qty error. limited-time-sale and free-home-shipping-event are of uncertain nature (the latter name strongly suggests a shipping-threshold promo page, not a product listing at all, and the former's name suggests a temporary campaign that might fail the Clearance test even if opened) - also not opened, also not rowed. RECOMMENDATION: re-run navigation discovery for sale-outdoor-living, sale-gifts, sale-furniture, limited-time-sale, and free-home-shipping-event in a later session/different network path once the DataDome block has cooled.
